body:
ARGUMENT AND CHOICE on bd-01M16BVT725FRQ6AN5GNA3A01W, before the edit. I am taking your option 2, but I want to SPLIT IT, because as stated the bead conflates two different things and adopting it literally would undo a guard that already works.

THE CONFLATION. "Defined on the supported subset" can mean either of two things, and they have opposite consequences:
(a) drop weighted components that have NO VALUE and sum the rest;
(b) include every component that HAS a value, and report the weakest support among them.

(a) IS THE DROP-AND-RENORMALIZE MOVE IN A NEW COSTUME. If a weighted component is Missing and the projection silently omits it, the scalar is no longer "w dot v over these components" - it is "w dot v over whichever components happened to be measured", which is a DIFFERENT LINEAR FUNCTIONAL wearing the same name and weights. Two signatures could return projections that are not comparable while both reporting version v0. That is precisely what MissingComponent already prevents, and it was the second half of the fix you accepted at 09:34. I am not undoing it.

(b) IS RIGHT AND IS WHAT I WILL BUILD. A weighted component with no value still REFUSES - unchanged. A component that has a value but rests on thin support still contributes, and the scalar publishes the MINIMUM support across contributing components, with the name of the component that set it. Your metaphor is the argument: a chain is no better supported than its thinnest link, and naming the link is what makes it actionable.

THE DISTINCTION UNDERNEATH, which I think is worth stating as a general rule rather than a projection detail: NO VALUE and LOW SUPPORT are different failures and deserve different answers. No value means we cannot compute the term at all - the honest response is to refuse, because any substitute is invention. Low support means we computed it from little evidence - the honest response is to publish it WITH the evidence, because refusing would discard a real measurement. Tonight's defects have almost all been the first mistake; this bead is about not over-correcting into refusing the second.

ONE HONEST GAP IN WHAT I CAN DELIVER. Only some components carry a support at all - compression, coherence, fidelity and the two step masses do, via MassRatio and StepMass. uniformCoverage, the mass fields and the rest are bare Doubles with no support notion, which is exactly bd-01M16E05TWX28QKJF2GFY67ZZV, the 14-field backlog. So the weakest-support figure can only be a minimum over the components that HAVE one. Rather than hide that, the result will also name the weighted components with NO support notion, so a reader sees "support 0.31, set by compression; 3 weighted components carry no support" instead of a bare 0.31 that overstates what is known. That list shrinks to empty as the backlog lands, and when it does the figure becomes a true minimum.

Implementing on that basis now. Reverse me on (b) versus (a) and I will rework it.
